clue.text: It should add spice to the journey!

definitions.text: It should add spice to the journey!

parts.words: It should add spice to the journey!
parts.note: to season food is to add spice, so the clue playfully pictures a seasoned travel pass that a commuter buys for regular trips

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a pass for travel that 'seasons' the trip: SEASON (add spice) and TICKET (for the journey).
explanation.definitionFit: A pass covering unlimited rail or bus trips over a set period is what a regular commuter buys for the journey.

clue.text: Burdened and confused by initial selection

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its opening letter, here the start of selection

parts.note: addled means muddled or confused

explanation.surface: Someone is weighed down and bewildered by the first choice they have to make.
explanation.definitionFit: To be saddled with something is to be lumbered or encumbered with it.

clue.text: Something worth having when fixed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
set means fixed or settled in place

explanation.surface: An object only becomes valuable once it has been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuable resource or useful quality is something worth having.

clue.text: Have they been left out from circular on religious outposts?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a circular shape is the letter O
missions are outposts set up by a church to spread its faith

explanation.surface: A question about whether some remote church stations were left off a mailing list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like a leaflet sent round; it gives the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Things omitted are those that have been left out or overlooked.

clue.text: Job request following termination of employment

indicators.note: the word for request comes after the letter taken from employment
the termination of a word is its final letter, here the end of employment

parts.note: to ask is to make a request

explanation.surface: A request for work made after someone has been sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work or a job to be done.

clue.text: A strike in London, eg, is a disaster

indicators.note: the letters for a strike go inside the word for London

parts.note: London is an example of a city
to lam is to hit or strike hard

explanation.surface: A walkout by workers in the capital is a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout by workers, but here it means a blow; 'in' puts it, with A, inside the London word.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a grave misfortune or catastrophe.

clue.text: Set out to cover team departures

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover, or surround, the team
out signals that the letters of set are rearranged

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A side is laid out to cover the ways people leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to ETS, and 'to cover' wraps those letters round the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits are acts of leaving, that is, departures.

clue.text: Cook, in a dream, created this!

definitions.text: Cook, in a dream, created this!

indicators.note: created signals that the letters of the words in a dream are made into something new

explanation.surface: A chef dreamt up a new recipe in their sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange IN A DREAM; the whole clue also describes the result, a steeping liquid a cook might invent.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned liquid in which a cook soaks meat or fish before cooking is a steeping sauce of that kind.

clue.text: Thin consommè a great part of it

indicators.note: the answer is only part of the stretch of words consommè a great

explanation.surface: A clear soup is mostly made of a thin broth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' looks like a description of consommé, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or lean, so thin in quantity.

clue.text: Miserable surroundings for one ship's sending off

indicators.note: the word for miserable surrounds the letters for one and ship

parts.note: dismal means gloomy or miserable
one is I as a Roman numeral
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Unhappy surroundings as a vessel is dispatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending off' is the football term: a player's dismissal from the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissal is a dispatching or ordering away, as in a red card in football.

clue.text: Impression of road being up a long time

indicators.note: in an across clue, up reverses the word for road

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, read here as letters M and I
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: An impression of a road under repair for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; the digit 1 doubles as I, and 'being up' reverses MI to IM.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or mental picture, an impression of something.

clue.text: Most recent city trial

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: The newest experiment carried out by a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest is the newest or most up to date.

clue.text: Wonderful start to Sunday — preparing potatoes!

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of Sunday

parts.note: mashing is one way of preparing potatoes

explanation.surface: A great start to the weekend's last day: mashing spuds for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is British slang for excellent or terrific.

clue.text: Pull over a particularly intimidating woman

parts.note: to drag is to pull
on can mean over or upon, as with a cloth on a table

explanation.surface: A driver is told to stop by an alarming woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull over' reads as a motoring command; it is split, with 'over' giving ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is informal for a fierce, domineering woman.

clue.text: Famous Greek mount crossed by experts

indicators.note: the word for experts runs across, or around, the word for mount

parts.note: aces are experts
a hill is a mount

explanation.surface: A celebrated Greek climbs a mountain that experts have traversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the great warrior hero of Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Enclosure for netting cod and skate

indicators.note: netting suggests fish caught and tumbled together, so the letters of cod and skate are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pen for keeping netted fish such as cod and skate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for netting cod and skate' looks like the purpose of the enclosure; 'netting' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a fenced enclosure of stakes.

clue.text: Tory examined and called into question

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
tested means examined

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is scrutinised and challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contested is disputed or challenged.

clue.text: Monkeys do better with paper

parts.note: to monkey about is to fool around, so monkeys means fools
to cap something is to top or outdo it

explanation.surface: Apes improve their performance using paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkeys' looks like animals but is a verb. Foolscap is a traditional British paper size.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a large size of writing or printing sheet.

clue.text: Choose, in another way, to find a logical connection

indicators.note: in another way says the letters of choose and in are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Picking differently to make an argument hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesion is the quality of fitting together into a unified, consistent whole.

clue.text: Opera for motor mechanics?

definitions.meaning: Bizet's opera about a Spanish gypsy
playfully, men who work on cars

explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's famous opera bears this title, and read as two words it whimsically names people who fix automobiles.

clue.text: Shows contempt when school head approaches noisily

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of school
noisily says the word for approaches is heard rather than read

parts.note: nears means approaches

explanation.surface: Pupils jeer loudly as the headteacher draws near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisily' signals a homophone: NEARS sounds like NEERS. 'head' looks like a headteacher but gives just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneering is showing scorn or derision.

clue.text: Leak from diocesan attendant?

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A news leak traced to a bishop's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the slow escape of liquid, a leak.

clue.text: Register presence of bread and cry

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread
a call is a cry or shout

explanation.surface: Proof that bread was there, and a shout to confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll call is the reading of names to record who is there.

clue.text: Get a grip on the hidden problem

explanation.definitionFit: To catch is to grasp hold of, and a catch is a concealed snag in an offer.

clue.text: Qualification obtained in 60 minutes

definitions.meaning: an academic award from a university
sixty minutes of arc make one unit of angle

explanation.surface: A diploma gained within an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A university award is one sense; sixty minutes of arc form one unit of angle in the other.

clue.text: Right to step up and cover the same ground again

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for step is read from the bottom

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: It is fine to step forward and go over old ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'step up' reads as a phrase meaning to come forward; 'up' reverses PACE to ECAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise again, going back over what was said.

clue.text: Trick about to take us in

indicators.note: the word for about takes the next word inside it
in confirms the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A con that is about to fool us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take us in' looks like being deceived, matching the definition, but it is the container signal around US.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a deception or stratagem.

clue.text: Former queen with time to make an effort

parts.note: ex means former
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch, given time, tries hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert oneself is to strive or apply effort.

clue.text: Prawns and lobster perhaps act as cure

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words act as cure might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Seafood offered as a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like it qualifies lobster as an example, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Crustacea is the class of shelled arthropods to which these seafoods belong.

clue.text: She sipped her tipple with this for lunch

definitions.text: She sipped her tipple with this for lunch

indicators.note: tipple hints at drink and tipsy disorder, so the letters of she sipped her are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman has a drink alongside her lunchtime dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange SHE SIPPED HER; the whole clue also describes a lunch eaten with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie of minced lamb topped with mashed potato is a classic British pub lunch.
